entries.definition: A player's place on the all-time board by CLR. The overall board ranks every lane together; each lane tab ranks players within that position.

Where a career's value was earned: every team, league and lane the player logged, each with the CLR earned there, highest first (e.g. T1 245.3, DAMWON Gaming 30.1). Each season's CLR is split in proportion to that season's LPS, plus the résumé points that season earned, so the pieces add up to the player's CLR. A player who changed teams mid-season has that whole season booked to their main team for the year, so the team split isn't exact for mid-season moves yet.

Career Legend Rating, the site's headline ranking: CLR = w_career × CareerVal + w_pace × PaceVal + w_peak × PeakVal + w_bonus × Résumé. Inspired by baseball's JAWS and hockey's PPS, it puts career bulk, per-season pace, peak and hardware (titles, placements, awards) on one scale, so longevity, rate, dominance and trophies all count. The current weights are shown at the top of this page.

The résumé bonus in CLR: w_bonus × (Intl + Titles + Awards). It rewards big-stage results the box score can't see. It's shown already weighted, as are Intl, Titles and Awards, so CareerVal + PaceVal + PeakVal + Résumé = CLR.

Placement points from every cross-region event LPS scores: Worlds, MSI, EWC, First Stand, MSC, LTA, Rift Rivals, ASI, IWCI, IEM, IPL, MLG, DreamHack and OGN 2012. Points are set per event and round (champion, finalist, semifinalist, quarterfinalist, group stage). A title's points follow the event's weight in LPS, anchored on Worlds and MSI, so it counts as much as the event mattered. Credited from the player's team's finish that year.
Domestic split-playoff titles and finals, each scaled by the strength of that region that year (an LCK or LPL title outweighs one from a weaker region), plus domestic cups (KeSPA Cup, Demacia Cup).

Individual awards, a small tiebreaker pulled from Leaguepedia: regional and season MVP, All-Pro 1st/2nd/3rd team, domestic Finals MVP, and at Worlds and MSI the Finals MVP, tournament MVP and All-Pro team. Domestic awards are scaled by region strength; Worlds and MSI honors are flat.

The résumé split into 14 categories, each with a count (#, how many the player earned across their career) and its weighted points (Pt). The points add up exactly to Résumé: the nine Worlds, MSI and other-international categories make Intl; domestic titles, finals and cups make Titles; MVP and All-Pro make Awards. Only achievements that score are counted (a title in an unrated region is worth 0, so it isn't listed), and points scale with region strength wherever the parent bonus does, so two titles can be worth different amounts.
Worlds championships won (count) and their points (flat, part of Intl).
Worlds finalist (runner-up) finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
Worlds semifinalist or quarterfinalist finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI championships won (count) and their points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI finalist (runner-up) finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).
MSI semifinalist finishes (count) and points (flat, part of Intl).

Other cross-region event titles (EWC, First Stand, Mid-Season Cup, LTA cross-conference, Rift Rivals, Asia Invitational, IWCI, IEM, IPL, MLG, DreamHack, OGN 2012) -- count and points. Champion points are derived from each event's LPS weight. Part of Intl.
Other cross-region event finalist finishes (count) and points (part of Intl).
Other cross-region event semifinalist or quarterfinalist finishes (count) and points (part of Intl).
Domestic split-playoff titles (count) and points (region-Elo scaled, part of Titles).
Domestic split-playoff runner-up finishes (count) and points (region-Elo scaled, part of Titles).
Domestic cup podiums -- KeSPA Cup (KR) + Demacia Cup (CN) (count) and points (weight-derived, part of Titles).
MVP-type awards -- regional/season MVP, Worlds/MSI tournament MVP, and any Finals MVP (count) and points (part of Awards).
All-Pro-team selections -- domestic 1st/2nd/3rd team and Worlds/MSI All-Pro (count) and points (part of Awards).

CLR's bulk term: w_career × (career LPS ÷ D), where D is a typical career length in years. Careers longer than D keep a proportional edge; shorter ones scale down. Shown already weighted, so the four CLR parts add up to CLR.

CLR's rate term: w_pace × LPS per active season, pulled toward the average player in proportion to how few games the player has (empirical-Bayes shrinkage). Brilliant short careers score well, but tiny, noisy samples can't top the board. It balances CareerVal, which rewards length. Shown already weighted.

CLR's peak term: w_peak × (the average of the player's peak years + a length bonus). The peak years are the player's best k seasons, with k chosen to maximize mean(top k) + bonus × (k-th best season) × (k − 1). A one-year peak scores exactly its best season; a long plateau scores its average plus a reward for length, and a season only joins the peak if it is close to the rest. A better season can never lower PeakVal.
How many seasons make up the player's peak, i.e. how wide the peak is. Always at least 1, since the best season always counts.
Mean LPS across the player's peak years (the height of the peak plateau). PeakVal builds on this by adding a length bonus for extra peak years.

High Noon peer rank: the player's best single-season standing, ranking that year's rated players by LPS (adjusted for schedule length), where 1 = best that year. Lane ranks within the player's position; Glob ranks across everyone. A companion metric, not part of CLR. Lower is better.

High Noon (3-year): the average peer rank across the player's three best-ranked seasons, wherever in the career they fall (not necessarily back to back), within the lane or across everyone. Measures dominance across a player's strongest seasons: about 1.0 means a clear #1 three times over. Lower is better; a companion metric, not part of CLR.
The seasons that make up HN3Lane / HN3Glob -- i.e. the player's 3 best-ranked years within lane / globally.

League Performance Score for a season: Baseline + Contribution + WinBonus, summed across regular season, playoffs and tournaments, so playing more games helps. Adjusted for schedule length, so a full season is worth the same in every year and the seasons add up to career LPS.
Average score per game (contribution + win bonus + baseline, where baseline only counts on series wins), with every game weighted equally. Unaffected by schedule length.

Stakes-weighted average score per game: playoff and tournament games count more, but it divides by the total weight, so it stays comparable across leagues. Higher than LPS/Gm means the player raised their game when more was on the line.
The contribution part of LPS per game (every game equal, on the LPS scale): how much of a player's per-game value comes from their win-probability contribution. Unaffected by schedule length.
Stakes-weighted contribution per game, weighted the same way as LPS/Gm·wt. Higher than Con/Gm means the player contributed more in bigger games.

Individual clutch: contribution per game in high-stakes matches minus contribution per game in the regular season, before the per-lane adjustment. High stakes means domestic playoffs and international events; international games count double, with extra weight by bracket stage (final 3×, semifinal 2×, quarterfinal 1.5×, group stage 1×). Small samples are pulled toward the typical player (Bayesian shrinkage worth 20 games) so a handful of games can't dominate. Positive = raised their game in big moments; negative = faded. Unlike Intangibles, this is the player's own number.

LPS earned in each phase. Regular & playoffs are length-normalized per region (a full run ~ one unit); tournaments are weighted by viewership and normalized so a full winning run = the tournament's weight.
Points for the strength of the opponent's league, so wins over stronger regions count for more.

Win probability the player added compared with an expected player at their position: how far the player's actual game stats moved the win-probability model, summed over games. Contribution is put on a common scale per lane across all years, so a 90th-percentile game, and the best season ever, are worth the same in every role. That removes the box-score bias against supports and junglers, so cross-lane and same-team comparisons are fair, while keeping real differences between lanes within a year.
Credit for actually winning compared with what the model expected: beta × (result − predicted win chance). Positive = won games the model rated as losses; negative = lost games it rated as wins.
Contribution split by stat source -- these sum to Contribution. First blood is credited to the FB getter (+) / victim (-).
Mean per-game net win-probability contribution (after per-lane normalization; comparable across roles).

A team-level number: how much more the team wins than its box score (KDA, damage, first blood) predicts, per game, which captures macro, shotcalling and closing out games. It's the same for all five teammates, so it says nothing about any one player.
Mean model win probability for the player's team-games (team strength).
Strength of schedule: mean opponent-league baseline faced (higher = tougher).
Share of games the player got first blood or was the first-blood victim.
Player's single-game best / worst net contribution (win-prob).
Distinct tournaments the player appeared in.
The strength of the player's home region that season (its league's year-end Elo, from international results). Higher = stronger region.
LPS earned at one specific tournament (WLDs = Worlds, EWC = Esports World Cup, KeSPA and DCup = the Korean and Chinese domestic cups). Together they add up to Tourneys.
